\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مقصد} (maqsad)}{مقصد (maqsad)}]{\fa{مقصد} (maqsad) — a destination}

\label{lesson:FA-C430-maqsad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a compartment, then the Persian for a rail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مقصد}}
\textbf{\fa{مقصد}} (\emph{maqsad}) — \textquotedblleft{}a destination\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مقصد} \fa{ما} \fa{یک} \fa{روستای} \fa{کوچک} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Maqsad-e mâ yek rustâ-ye kuchek ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our destination is a small village.
\end{quote}

Arabic plural \emph{maqâsed}. The starting point is \emph{mabda'}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{maqsad} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{maqṣad}, which EtymDB lists; it is usually glossed 'the place one aims at', and it shares its root with \emph{qasd} 'intention'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maqsad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{maqsad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a compartment, then the Persian for a rail, then say \emph{maqsad} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تاخیر} (ta'khir)}{تاخیر (ta'khir)}]{\fa{تاخیر} (ta'khir) — a delay}

\label{lesson:FA-C430-takhir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a rail, then the Persian for a destination.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تاخیر}}
\textbf{\fa{تاخیر}} (\emph{ta'khir}) — \textquotedblleft{}a delay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قطار} \fa{ما} \fa{دو} \fa{ساعت} \fa{تاخیر} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Qatâr-e mâ do sâ'at ta'khir dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our train is two hours late.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bâ ta'khir} — late, delayed. \emph{Ta'khir dârad} — it is running late.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ta'khir} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{taʾḫīr}, which EtymDB lists; it is usually glossed 'putting off, delay'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a rail, then the Persian for a destination, then say \emph{ta'khir} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لغو} \fa{شدن} (laghv shodan)}{لغو شدن (laghv shodan)}]{\fa{لغو} \fa{شدن} (laghv shodan) — to be cancelled}

\label{lesson:FA-C430-laghv-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a destination, then the Persian for a delay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لغو} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{لغو} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{laghv shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be cancelled\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قطار} \fa{امشب} \fa{لغو} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Qatâr-e emshab laghv shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Tonight's train was cancelled.
\end{quote}

\emph{laghv} 'cancellation' + \emph{shodan}. The active verb is \emph{laghv kardan} — to cancel.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{laghv shodan} is built from \emph{laghv} 'annulment', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{laġw} 'idle talk, something of no effect' (EtymDB lists the Arabic word without a gloss), and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a destination, then the Persian for a delay, then say \emph{laghv shodan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دیر} \fa{کردن} (dir kardan)}{دیر کردن (dir kardan)}]{\fa{دیر} \fa{کردن} (dir kardan) — to be late, to run late}

\label{lesson:FA-C430-dir-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a delay, then the Persian for to be cancelled.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دیر} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{دیر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{dir kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be late, to run late\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اتوبوس} \fa{امروز} \fa{نیم} \fa{ساعت} \fa{دیر} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Otobus emruz nim sâ'at dir kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Today the bus was half an hour late.
\end{quote}

\emph{dir} 'late' + \emph{kardan}. Present stem \emph{kon-}: \emph{dir mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dir kardan} is built from native \emph{dir} 'late, long', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{dēr}, and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dir kardan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a delay, then the Persian for to be cancelled, then say \emph{dir kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بلندگو} (bolandgu)}{بلندگو (bolandgu)}]{\fa{بلندگو} (bolandgu) — a loudspeaker}

\label{lesson:FA-C430-bolandgu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be cancelled, then the Persian for to be late.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بلندگو}}
\textbf{\fa{بلندگو}} (\emph{bolandgu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a loudspeaker\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{بلندگو} \fa{اسم} \fa{ایستگاه} \fa{بعدی} \fa{را} \fa{گفتند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Az bolandgu esm-e istgâh-e ba'di râ goftand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They announced the name of the next station over the loudspeaker.
\end{quote}

\emph{boland} 'loud, high' + \emph{gu} 'saying', from \emph{goftan} (present stem \emph{gu-}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bolandgu} is a native compound of inherited words: \emph{boland} 'high, loud', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{buland}, and \emph{gu}, the present stem of \emph{goftan} 'to say': a thing that speaks loudly.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be cancelled, then the Persian for to be late, then say \emph{bolandgu} again
